timelineEvents.title: Jazz Piano Partnership
timelineEvents.label: 1928 · Jazz piano partnership
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper records jazz-influenced piano duo arrangements with Hermann Bick for Polydor.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Along with Hermann Bick (Bieck), he records piano duo arrangements for Deutsche Grammophon/Polydor. These sessions showcase contemporary American jazz standards including "Miss Annabelle Lee," "The Varsity Drag," and "The Song Is Ended." The collaboration blends classical virtuosity with jazz spontaneity, creating sophisticated interpretations that avoid the trivial "novelty piano" style of the era.

places.authorizedName: Kabarett der Komiker / KadeKo, probable July 1928 venue: Haus Cumberland / Palmenhaus, Kurfürstendamm 193–194, Berlin-Charlottenburg
places.publicNote: Berlin cabaret venue connected with Kaper’s paid work as a pianist. A July 1928 programme lists Sula Lewitsch and Bronisław Kaper as “Jazz auf zwei Klavieren”; because the event predates the later WOGA venue, Haus Cumberland / Palmenhaus at Kurfürstendamm 193–194 is retained as the probable site.
